overview: White sets up d3, c3 and f4 against the Sicilian regardless of Black replies. The usual plan is Nf3, Be2, 0-0, then e5 or a kingside push, while Black strikes in the centre with ...e5 or ...g6 and ...Bg7. A flexible anti-Sicilian that avoids the Open Sicilian theory.

white_ideas.idea: Play Nf3, Be2, 0-0 and f4-f5 or e5 as Black commits
Keep a compact centre with c3, d3 and f4

black_ideas.idea: Use the c-file and queenside space

typical_structures.structure: White clamp pawns c3, d3, e4, f4

character.notes: A slow set-up with kingside pawn play but rarely forcing.

structure.notes: White pawns c3/d3/e4/f4 and the centre is not yet resolved.

approach.notes: A set-up that can be played against many Black set-ups.

character.reason: White builds a clamp and attacks slowly; it is neither hard to break nor fast.

structure.reason: The centre is decided later and f4 can lead either to e5 or to a tension.

approach.reason: The c3/d3/f4 formation can be played against most Black set-ups.

level.reason: Plans matter more than concrete lines.

plans.reason: The pawn clamp supports a later kingside push.
